title: versioned-a-b-playground-and-rollback-orchestrator
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need a unified, low-friction way to run A/B and canary experiments across model versions with transparent exposure controls, sequential statistical checks, and automated remediation (auto-rollback or traffic throttling) when quality or latency regressions are detected. Current ad-hoc scripts and manual traffic splits are error-prone and make it hard to meet enterprise SLAs.

Objective: Ship an "A/B Playground" that lets engineering and product teams declare experiments for model variants, configure exposure schedules, choose statistical tests and significance thresholds, and define automated remediation policies. The system should support: staged rollouts (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%), shadow trials, paired (within-user) evaluation, and time-aware sequential checks that account for baseline drift and multiple comparisons.

Scope: this ticket focuses on product and orchestration design plus API/console spec for first MVP; engineering tickets will split runtime routing, metrics pipeline, and remediation executor. Design will contribute UX for experiment creation and visualization.

Key trade-offs considered: 
- Strict statistical guarantees vs time-to-detect: tighter alpha reduces false-alarms but delays detection; we propose configurable alpha with a sane default tuned for product use (default alpha=0.01 for primary metrics).
- Heavyweight per-request instrumentation for paired tests vs sample-efficiency: paired tests require attaching user keys to signals; provide optional paired-mode when identity is available.
- Automatic rollback aggressiveness: immediate 100% rollback vs graduated throttling; prefer graduated throttling for customer continuity with option for hard rollback for critical regressions.

High-level design summary: 
1) Experiment DSL (API + Console) - declarative JSON/YAML for experiment definition: variants, traffic plan, metrics (primary/secondary), statistical method (sequential t-test, Bayesian lift with posterior credible intervals, or nonparametric bootstrapping), stopping/rollback policy, observation window, and required sample size or power target.
2) Exposure controller - policy engine that enforces the percent of live traffic per variant per interval, allowing hold/advance/manual override and automatic progression on passing checks.
3) Metric ingestion & aggregator - a metrics pipeline that can compute per-variant aggregates and paired comparisons in near real-time (1 minute granularity) and feed the statistics engine.
4) Statistical engine - supports sequential testing with multiple comparison correction (Benjamini-Hochberg for families of metrics), drift-aware baseline recalibration, and posterior monitoring for Bayesian workflows.
5) Remediation executor - when a metric crosses a configured alarm threshold, take actions configured in the experiment: reduce exposure by X%, revert variant to baseline, mute variant and notify owners, or shadow-only.
6) Console/Reporting - timeline view with exposure history, metric traces with confidence intervals, p-value evolution, and an actions log with who approved advances/rollbacks.

Success metrics: 
- Time to detect a 5% regression on primary metric reduced by 30% vs manual rollouts.
- 95% of rollbacks created by auto-remediation are confirmed by engineering playbooks (fewer false positives).
- Customers can create and run a basic experiment in <15 minutes.

Out-of-scope for MVP: per-token content QA (L1 safety) checks and per-customer privacy-preserving metrics (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: API to create an experiment with variants, traffic schedule, primary metric, and rollback policy is available in Redwood API (documented).
Console 'New Experiment' flow wireframe implemented and validated by design review.
Exposure controller can enforce scheduled ramp from 0.1% to 100% and support manual pause/advance/rollback via API.
Statistical engine supports at least two modes: sequential frequentist test with alpha and Bayesian posterior monitoring; results surfaced in console and via webhook.
Remediation executor can run three actions: throttle-down (percent), full-rollback (switch all traffic back to baseline), and notify with a reproducible incident link.
Demo run with internal model variants showing auto-throttle on injected latency regression and successful manual override acceptance by SREs.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Miguel Torres: Initial draft of API objects attached to PRD. Need engineering estimates for pipeline cost; preferring 1min aggregation window. Action: Eng to evaluate cost and storage impact.
2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (Design): Wireframes for console flow uploaded. Suggest inline quickstart templates for 'canary', 'A/B test', and 'shadow-only' presets to reduce mistakes.

2026-03-04 - Lucas Meyer (SRE): Concern about automatic rollback causing flapping during noisy hours. Proposal: add cooldown period and require consecutive windows (e.g., 3) crossing threshold before hard rollback.

2026-03-05 - Asha Patel: Agreed with cooldown; add configuration default cooldown=3 windows and minimum observation period of 30 minutes for production experiments. Update acceptance criteria accordingly.

2026-03-06 - Miguel Torres: Engineering split created: ENG-21098 (routing + exposure controller), ENG-21100 (metrics pipeline + aggregation), ENG-21105 (statistical engine), ENG-21107 (remediation executor).
2026-03-08 - Compliance: Please confirm user-identifying keys won't be persisted beyond aggregation TTL when paired tests enabled. Added privacy checklist to follow-up tasks.

2026-03-09 - Miguel Torres: Prototype demo scheduled for 2026-03-22 with internal alpha customers (platform team). Added smoke tests scenario: simulate 7% quality regression on responses and measure detection time and rollback actions.
notes: Implementation notes: prefer incremental rollout. Start with server-side routing flags that read experiment config from central control plane, avoiding per-request DB hits by caching policies in edge routers.

Statistical considerations: report both p-values and effect-size with confidence intervals; use false-discovery-rate correction when multiple metrics are declared. Provide power calculators in the UI to recommend ramp durations and sample sizes.
Observability: attach experiment id to traces and logs; add a dedicated dashboard showing variant-level latency and quality percentiles and an experiment health badge for Console home.
SRE runbook stub: on auto-rollback, create incident with rollback rationale and a 'replay' job to re-run the experiment on shadow traffic for post-mortem.
